No. With the Moon at an altitude of **−51.9°**, it is far below your horizon—indeed, on the other side of the Earth relative to Perth—so it cannot be seen from your location at that time.

The other details would make it difficult even if it were above the horizon:

- **5.75% illuminated**: a very thin crescent.
- **Only 27.7° from the Sun**: it would be near the Sun in the sky, generally visible only around twilight if its altitude were favorable.
- But the decisive factor is altitude: **negative altitude means below the geometric horizon**, and −52° is nowhere close to rising.

So despite clear, dark conditions, there is no chance of seeing it at **19:25 AWST on 12 July 2026** from Perth.
